event.label: Votes on joining Russia
event.description: Start of the September 23–27 votes organized in Russian-controlled parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson. This graph compares article claims, not independently verified voting outcomes.

topics.label: Are the votes lawful?
topics.scope_note: Compare the same legal act. Holding votes and later taking Ukrainian land into Russia are separate acts. Red marks opposing legal claims, not a ruling by this graph.

topics.label: Can people choose freely?
topics.scope_note: Keep cities, speakers and times separate. A promise of safe voting is not proof that voting was safe; a calm scene does not prove free choice.

topics.label: How is voting carried out?
topics.scope_note: Compare voting arrangements and assessments of their quality. Home visits alone do not prove threats; in-person voting is not automatically the same as polling-station voting.

topics.label: Support, turnout and results
topics.scope_note: A poll answer, turning out to vote and an announced result are different measures. A majority intending to vote yes is not proof of a free vote.

topics.label: What could happen next?
topics.scope_note: These claims describe possible future actions after Russia claims the land. They are not reports that those later events already happened.

topics.label: Threats of economic penalties
topics.scope_note: Preparing new penalties is different from judging whether older penalties worked. Agreement concerns the named sources’ policy direction, not the whole outlet.

topics.label: Words used for the votes
topics.scope_note: Opposing descriptions such as occupied and liberated are coded as framing clashes, not proof that a factual question has been settled. A quoted view is separate from the outlet’s own wording.

edges.reason: The FT narrator presents the vote through occupation and repression. Putin, quoted by Izvestia, presents Russia as responding to residents’ sincere wish to decide their own lives. The passages assign contrasting agency to residents.
edges.caveat: The FT qualifies its assessment as applying to many residents. Putin’s broad account of residents’ wishes is a quoted justification. Human review must align their populations and scope.
edges.direction_reason: FT02 is proposed to contradict the framing in I05. The arrow follows the analyst-assigned comparison order.

edges.label: Intimidation and coercion versus Protection and security
edges.reason: The Ukrainian adviser quoted by CNN describes armed home visits as coercion at gunpoint. The Russia-appointed official quoted by the FT describes police-accompanied visits as protection. The security presence is given opposing meanings.
edges.caveat: The CNN allegation concerns Mariupol and was not independently verified. The FT official discusses Zaporizhzhia. This compares the lens on similar practices across places, rather than asserting the same team or incident.
edges.direction_reason: CNN02 is proposed to contradict the framing in FT05. The arrow follows the analyst-assigned comparison order.

edges.label: Below democratic standards versus Open and transparent preparation
edges.shared_focus: The quality and legitimacy of the voting arrangements
edges.reason: The FT narrator judges the methods against democratic standards and finds them deficient. Matviyenko, quoted by TASS, praises organization, transparency and openness. They select different standards to evaluate the voting exercise.
edges.caveat: Administrative preparation and democratic fairness can differ. Matviyenko partly relays colleagues’ views. The proposed conflict concerns the evaluative lens.
edges.direction_reason: FT09 is proposed to contradict the framing in T03. The arrow follows the analyst-assigned comparison order.

edges.label: An imposed exercise run by occupiers and puppets versus A historic act of residents’ free will
edges.source_lens: An imposed exercise run by occupiers and puppets
edges.target_lens: A historic act of residents’ free will
edges.shared_focus: The agency and legitimacy assigned to the vote
edges.reason: Censor.NET’s narrator uses occupiers, puppets and so-called referendum. Saulenko, quoted by the FT, describes a historic expression of free will and a bright future. The descriptions center imposed control and voluntary choice respectively.
edges.caveat: Censor.NET’s lead names Donetsk, Luhansk and Melitopol. Saulenko speaks from Berdyansk. His praise is separate from the FT’s own assessment and concerns a different local setting.
edges.direction_reason: CEN05 is proposed to contradict the framing in FT01. The arrow follows the analyst-assigned comparison order.

edges.label: Manufactured outcomes versus Authentic popular will
edges.shared_focus: Whether the vote can supply a genuine popular mandate
edges.reason: Jean-Pierre, quoted by Kyiv Independent, pre-labels Russia’s announced outcomes fabricated. Putin, quoted by Izvestia, justifies the vote as a response to residents’ sincere wishes. The framing shifts the source of legitimacy from manufactured results to popular agency.
edges.caveat: A predicted result and a claim about residents’ wishes are different propositions. This is a proposed legitimacy-frame conflict, requiring review of whose wishes and which results are meant.
edges.direction_reason: KI02 is proposed to contradict the framing in I05. The arrow follows the analyst-assigned comparison order.

edges.label: Armed pressure limits residents’ choice supports Voting under occupation is far from free choice
edges.target_lens: Voting under occupation is far from free choice
edges.shared_focus: Whether residents can freely choose during the September 23–27 votes
edges.reason: The Ukrainian mayoral adviser’s account in CNN places armed men alongside door-to-door voting teams and describes coercion. That allegation gives a concrete reason for the restricted-choice lens expressed by the FT narrator.
edges.support_scope: The framing of constrained voter agency in the reported setting.
edges.caveat: CNN could not independently verify the adviser’s account, and the adviser was outside Mariupol. This does not establish coercion throughout all four regions or make CNN the author of the allegation.
edges.direction_reason: CNN02 reinforces the named part of FT02’s framing. Direction records the analyst’s proposed support relation, not a response between articles.

edges.label: An individual voter expects to have no meaningful influence supports Announced outcomes will be manufactured
edges.source_lens: An individual voter expects to have no meaningful influence
edges.shared_focus: Whether the announced results will meaningfully depend on residents’ participation and choices
edges.reason: The Donetsk businessman’s expectation that a vote will be counted even if he does not participate presents the result as detached from his agency. That account reinforces the manufactured-outcome lens in Jean-Pierre’s statement reported by Kyiv Independent.

edges.caveat: An unnamed individual’s expectation in Donetsk is not proof of how votes were counted, and cannot verify Jean-Pierre’s broader prediction about every announced outcome. These are attributed views, not endorsements by both outlets.

edges.source_lens: Observation is foregrounded as part of the voting process

edges.target_lens: Claimed incorporation could raise Russia’s response stakes

edges.reason: Peskov’s statement in CNN supplies the territorial reclassification behind the escalation lens: Russia would regard Ukrainian efforts to retake the regions as attacks on Russian territory. That stated position gives a reason for the Global Times expert’s forecast of a wider range of possible Russian responses.

Peskov’s classification does not establish legal sovereignty, justify a response, or confirm the expert’s prediction that Russia might use every possible military and political means.
